reason: Conversation 1 clearly discourages DIY regassing, correctly reads the evidence (no frost, cold-less back wall, barely warm condenser, knife damage, oily mark) as a sealed-system leak, and gives sensible cost advice: replacement is likely cheapest, with an optional engineer diagnostic. It also covers R600a flammability with ventilation and ignition-source advice. Conversation 2 wanders through low-value checks (dusty coils, door seals) despite clear evidence of a sealed-system fault, never gives a firm diagnosis or addresses cost or replacement, and suggests waiting 24 hours with doors shut, which wastes time and risks food safety.
